race_context: Union Township School Corporation (UTSC) serves Union Township in Porter County. Its central office is at 599 W 300 N, Valparaiso {ut_board_page}. It runs four schools: John Simatovich Elementary (JSE), Union Center Elementary (UCE), Union Township Middle School (UTMS) and Wheeler High School (WHS) {ut_board_page}. Leigh Barnes is superintendent, and Allen Cochran is assistant superintendent of finance {ut_ref_article}. The district calls itself a small school district {ut_finance}. This guide did not find a current enrollment count on the district's pages.

Board: the district lists five members for 2026: Christine Kostbade (president), Kevin Ribordy (vice president), Leah Pagone (secretary), Lori McLaughlin (deputy secretary) and Bob Tichy {ut_members}. Members are paid $2,000 a year, plus $112 for each regular meeting and $62 for each special meeting or executive session {ut_remun}. Seats on the 2026 ballot are District 2, District 4 and one at-large seat, each 'vote for 1' {in_list}. Kostbade, Ribordy and Pagone all won Union Township school board races in 2022 {lpm_2022}. That report did not say which seat each won.

Who is running: Kostbade (no party affiliation) faces Mark A. Werno (Republican) in District 2. Pagone (no party affiliation) faces Jocelyn Prue (Independent) in District 4. Ribordy (no party affiliation) is unopposed for the at-large seat {in_list}. This guide did not find the district's map of board districts or its rules for how members are elected.

Referendum on the same ballot: the board is asking voters to renew the operating referendum first passed in 2013 and renewed in 2020 {ut_finance}{ut_faq}. The ballot question asks for up to eight years at a rate of no more than $0.35 per $100 of assessed value, raising at most $3,374,291 a year. By the state-required formula, that adds $681 a year for a median $400,000 home {dlgf_ut}. The state reviewed the ballot language on June 24, 2026 {dlgf_ut}. The board's June 23 agenda listed a 'Finance and Referendum Update' and 'Consideration of Referendum Tax Levy Resolution' {ut_ag_2026_06_23}.

District's case for the referendum: the district's FAQ says the current rate is 21 cents and expires if voters take no action. It says SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law, cuts local revenue by about $12 million over eight years, and that without renewal the district 'stands to lose more than $2.7 million each year beginning in 2027' {ut_faq}. The district plans a rate of $0.31 in 2027 {ut_faq}. It estimates the referendum would raise up to $3.0 million a year: $1.25 million for attracting and keeping teachers and staff, $1.0 million for class sizes, $500,000 for academic programs and $250,000 for safety {ut_faq}. A superintendent presentation says UTSC is in 'the bottom 7%' of districts in state basic grant per student {ut_slides}. The district lists cuts it would consider if the referendum fails, including middle school and JV athletics, elementary media specialists and nurses, band and choir, preschool, STEM electives, counselors, elementary school resource officers, theater and transportation {ut_ref_page}. A separate group, Friends of Union Township Schools, is campaigning for a yes vote {ut_faq}.

Facilities: in fall 2025 the board pursued a progressive design-build project. It adopted a one-proposer resolution on Oct. 15 {ut_ag_2025_10_15} and selected a design-builder on Nov. 12 {ut_ag_2025_11_12}. On Feb. 18, 2026 it took up a contract amendment to proceed to Step 2 with Performance Services Inc. {ut_ag_2026_02_18}. The district says recent debt-funded work includes renovating Union Center Elementary and the athletic fields, updating UTMS hallways and lighting, and repairing the brick facade at John Simatovich {ut_finance}. The FAQ says 'No teaching positions have been lost because of past or current building projects' {ut_faq}.

Budget and staff: the board adopted the 2026 budget and a teachers' contract (the UTTA collective bargaining agreement) on Oct. 15, 2025 {ut_ag_2025_10_15}. It considered raises for administrators and non-certified staff on Dec. 17 {ut_ag_2025_12_17}. A budget hearing and the naming of a collective bargaining team were on the Sept. 16, 2026 agenda {ut_ag_2026_09_16}.

Other 2026 items: a presentation on Indiana's new K-12 accountability model (March 17) {ut_ag_2026_03_17}; adoption of a wireless devices policy (June 23) {ut_ag_2026_06_23}; and an extra eLearning day added for the May election day for student and staff safety (Feb. 18) {ut_ag_2026_02_18}.
Forums: this guide found no candidate forums, questionnaires or news coverage of these races.
